device.description: 10-bit 3 MSPS micro-power SAR ADC with SPI-compatible serial output
device.note: ads7885.pdf (SLAS567) p.3 ADS7884 specifications (full-scale 0 to VDD, VDD 2.7-5.5 V), p.6-7 timing requirements (td1 15 ns, td2 20 ns, td4 15 ns max at 3 V), p.7 device information and terminal functions, p.7-8 ADS7884 normal operation (Figure 1: 2 leading zeros, 10 data bits, 4 lagging zeros), p.8-9 power-down mode (Figures 3-4)

pages: p.3 (specs), p.6-7 (timing), p.7 (pinout, terminal functions), p.7-8 (normal operation, Figure 1), p.8-9 (power-down, Figures 3-4)
notModeled: analog input (0 V to VDD; VDD is also the reference); the conversion is clocked by SCLK (not timed: the result is the 0 V code at once)

frame: the first zero is clocked out by the CS falling edge and each SCLK falling edge shifts the next bit (read on the rising edge): SPI mode 0 shape; SDO goes 3-state after the 16th SCLK falling edge (idle "z") or at CS rising

power-down: CS high after the 2nd and before the 10th SCLK falling edge powers the device down; a dummy frame of at least 10 SCLK falling edges wakes it (power-up time 0.8 us); frames during wake-up return invalid data
CS high before the end of the conversion aborts it (SDO 3-state; no valid data in the next frame)
digital inputs may go up to 5.5 V regardless of VDD (p.7); not expressed (vcc max is 5.5 V)
quiet time tq, acquisition time and SCLK frequency limits; delays at VDD = 3 V (the maximum) are used
variants: ads7885.pdf covers ADS7884 (10-bit) and ADS7885 (8-bit): same pinout and timing, frame 2 leading zeros + data + lagging zeros to 16 bits; ADS7883 is the 12-bit version
